title: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure: Ward Guide

numbers.context: Repeat reassessment and thiazide escalation window
Urinary sodium at 6 h predicts diuretic resistance

negations.phrase: Warm and dry needs no decongestion
negations.rule: Warm and dry profile requires no decongestion
40 mg IV start applies to diuretic-naive patients
Inotropes are reserved for cardiogenic shock, never congestion alone

negations.phrase: Do not give fluids for a low blood pressure that comes with congestion
negations.rule: Never give fluid boluses for hypotension with congestion

negations.phrase: Do not stop beta blockers abruptly unless there is shock
negations.rule: Keep beta blockers unless shock is present

conditions.phrase: when the response is poor after 6 hours
conditions.rule: Add a thiazide only when response is poor after 6 h
Nitrates are first line only when blood pressure permits
Do not stop beta blockers abruptly unless shock
Check potassium and renal function after every diuretic dose change

highYield.fact: Bedside triad: dyspnoea, orthopnoea, elevated JVP
BNP >100 pg/mL supports diagnosis; obesity lowers it, renal failure raises it
Classify perfusion x congestion within 1 hour (Warm/Cold x Wet/Dry)
IV furosemide 40 mg if naive, or double home oral dose if already on loop diuretic
Urinary sodium <50 mmol/L at 6 h predicts diuretic resistance; add thiazide if poor response at 6 h
Inotropes only for cardiogenic shock, not congestion alone
Never give fluids for low BP with congestion; never stop beta blockers abruptly unless shock
